references.text: Parallel text describing Bezalel's ability to devise artistic works in gold, silver, and bronze - same wording and content as Exodus 35:32
Previous verse explaining that God filled Bezalel with His Spirit, with wisdom and understanding, which is the basis for the abilities described in verse 32
Describes how Bezalel and Oholiab carried out the work with wisdom and understanding as the Lord had given them to serve in the tabernacle ministry
God gives a spirit of wisdom to craftsmen to make Aaron's priestly garments - same principle of divine empowerment for artistic work
Hiram from Tyre was filled with wisdom and understanding to perform all work in bronze - similar divine empowerment for metalwork
Solomon asks for a skilled man who can work in gold, silver, and bronze for the temple construction - same metals mentioned
Huram-Abi is described as skilled in working with gold, silver, bronze, and iron - parallel to Bezalel's abilities with precious metals
Specifies how the given ability for 'artistic work' was carried out in practice through the making of the priestly garments.
Thematic parallel showing the continuity in the need for artistic craftsmanship for God's house from the tabernacle to the temple.
Complementary verse that completes the description of Bezalel's total artistic gifts from God's Spirit.
